title: Audit event capture guidelines: field-level deltas and SAML identity linking
creator: Ava Morales
description: Scope: Define a pragmatic, storage- and query-friendly audit event schema and event taxonomy focused on administrative actions for RBAC v2. This ticket covers: (1) field-level delta encoding for admin operations (what changed, who changed it, and contextual metadata), (2) canonical actor identity linking for SSO/SAML events (linking SAML assertions to internal principals and fallback heuristics), and (3) minimal searchable index fields for rapid incident triage. Goals: make post-hoc forensic analysis reliable, enable efficient retention/archival policies, and make audit events consumable by the Console and incident playbooks. Constraints: avoid duplicating large payloads, keep event size bounded for high-throughput write paths, support partial redaction for PII, and keep the schema backwards-compatible with existing lookup tooling where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Schema document published with top-level fields: event_id, timestamp, action, resource_type, resource_id, actor (canonical), actor_source, actor_display, target (optional), before_delta, after_delta, change_summary, request_id, client_ip, auth_context, trace_id, retention_tier
Delta format defined to represent field-level changes using list-of-tuples (field_path, op, before, after) with ops: added|removed|modified|unchanged. Example provided.

SAML linking rules documented: primary = mapped internal user_id from SAML NameID/attributes, secondary heuristics = matching email alias + identity-provider-id, and fallbacks when SAML assertion missing or ambiguous.
Indexing spec created for Console queries: which fields are indexed, suggested analyzers, and maximum index cardinality guidelines
Implementation guide with write-path considerations (sampling, batching, size limits) and a migration plan for existing audit consumers
Security review completed and signed off; redaction rules for sensitive attributes recorded
work_log: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Ava Morales to consolidate field-level delta design with SAML identity linking requirements.
2025-02-11: Spike: measured average admin action payloads from last 30 days (median 1.2KB, 95p 12KB). Noted a small tail of large policy blobs.
2025-02-12: Engineering sync: agree to cap per-event payload to 16KB in hot path; larger payloads go to object storage with reference URL in event.
2025-02-12: Design review with Security: require explicit redaction markers and allow redaction at event creation. Security requested a 'sensitive_fields' hint array.
2025-02-13: PM feedback (Lina Chen): add retention_tier and customer_impact fields; include example UI mappings for Console.
2025-02-14: Rohit started a draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-schema/pull/87 - includes schema draft and example encoding. Requested review from @security-team and @console-observability.
2025-02-14: Decided to represent deltas as ordered arrays to preserve human-readable change order rather than unordered maps.
2025-02-14: Note: will reuse existing event_id /trace_id conventions to ensure correlation with traces and logs.
decision_log: Delta encoding: use explicit field_path strings (dot-notation) and ops {added, removed, modified, unchanged}. This keeps events compact and queryable without nested diffs.
Large payloads: store full resource snapshots in S3-like object store with signed short-lived reference in the event under resource_snapshot_url; snapshots default to retention tier 'archival'.

SAML canonicalization: first try mapping NameID -> internal user_id via identity-provider mapping table; if missing, attempt attribute-based mapping (email) and finally record saml_assertion_summary (hash + issuer) when no mapping found.
Indexing policy: index event_id, timestamp, action, resource_type, resource_id, actor, actor_source, change_summary (keyword), and retention_tier. Do not index full before/after blobs.
